 Follow Harry Shum Jr. Heard Three Words From His Mom For The First Time At 44 After ‘DWTS’
 Kelly Coffey-Behrens Tue, November 17, 2026 at 8:20 PM UTC 5 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. TPI/MEGA Harry Shum Jr . and Jenna Johnson brought "Mary Poppins" to the ballroom on "Dancing with the Stars," but the moment the "Glee" alum is still thinking about happened over the phone. While catching up with his mom after Disney Night, Shum got a surprisingly detailed review of his performance and heard three words she'd never said to him before. The "Grey's Anatomy" star shared the story in a November 15 Instagram video, explaining why a conversation that started with dance steps and ended with a quick goodnight meant so much to him.
 Harry Shum Jr. Recalls The First Time His Mom Said 'I Love You'
 RCF / MEGA
 Shum's mom had been telling him how much she enjoyed watching him dance when she offered a little advice. She told him to keep going and do his best. Then, as she was getting ready to hang up, she said something that caught him completely off guard.
 "Then, in the end, she started telling me, like, 'You know what, just keep going, do your best, that's all that matters.' And then she said, 'Okay, I know you're tired. I love you, goodnight.' If you know, you know. In certain cultures, your parents just never say that, they just show it," he recalled. "And to say 'I love you' unlocked something in me."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Shum shared what it felt like to finally hear those words at 44. "Forty-four years later, hearing 'I love you' for the first time from your mom. That is growth. I just wanted to share that with you guys."
 His 'Mary Poppins' Routine Got His Mom Talking
 View this post on Instagram 
 A post shared by Dancing With The Stars #DWTS (@dancingwiththestars) 
 For Disney Night, Shum and Johnson performed a jazz routine to "Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious." His mom had plenty to say about the number, down to details he was surprised she'd picked up on. Shum said he'd never heard her talk that closely about anything he'd done.
 The comparison that stuck with him came from her own life. His mom is a painter, and she told him that watching the routine made her feel the way she does when she paints. It gave Shum a chance to hear what his performance had brought out in someone who usually expressed herself through her own art.

 Shum Explains Why Those Three Words Meant So Much
 RCF / MEGA
 In the caption, Shum described his mother as "an incredible mom who has shown me love in every way except with these three words." He explained that saying it out loud simply wasn't a habit in their household. "It's just not what we grew up saying to each other, like kryptonite. BUT I heard it last night, and I guess I'm not the only one growing while being on 'DWTS' but so is my mom," he wrote.
 Advertisement Advertisement Shum also thought about people who might see their own families in his story. "It might not seem like a big deal, but this is for me, and I know for many others as well who have never experienced their parents say these words out loud."
 His Mom's Advice Prompted A Thank-You To Fans
 KAT / MEGA
 Shum's mom also told him he was "bringing a lot of people joy." That piece of their conversation prompted him to thank fans who have been cheering him and Johnson on throughout Season 35. The pair were among the six couples still in the competition when he shared the video.
 "That's what really makes me happy, that you guys are out there spreading love. That says a lot about you," he said. "I get to be able to entertain. And you guys are giving a lot back to me as well. So I really appreciate it. I love you guys, and just like my mom said to me, I'll say it again: I love y'all. Thank you."
 Harry Shum Jr. Brings A 'Glee' Throwback To The 'DWTS' Semifinals
 KAT / MEGA
 After the "Mary Poppins" routine that got his mom talking, Harry Shum Jr. is heading into tonight's "Dancing with the Stars" semifinals with a number that goes back to his "Glee" days . He and Jenna Johnson will dance a quickstep to "Valerie," a song Shum first danced to on "Glee" while his late co-star Naya Rivera sang lead. This time, the "DWTS" band will perform the show's version live in the ballroom.
